newsitem.title: ITALY: Controllers' strike disrupts air travel in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Controllers' strike disrupts air travel in Italy.

text.p: A union representing air traffic controllers in Italy held a four-hour strike on Friday and the national airline Alitalia said its services were severely disrupted.

The strike, which began at midday (1000 GMT), was called by the CISAL union to protest against alleged failure by management of the Italian air traffic authority to consult workers' representatives on restructuring plans.
Other unions in the sector did not take part.
Alitalia said in a statement that its flights from Rome's Fiumicino airport faced delays of up to two hours and that the protest would cause severe disruption at other Italian airports.
It said its image and income were being damaged by industrial action which did not directly concern the company.
The controllers' strike coincided with a national one-day strike called by unions seeking higher pay for Italy's engineering and metalworkers.
That stoppage was also expected to hit air travel, with maintenance engineers and technicians asked to down tools at all Italian airports for their normal three eight-hour shifts.
